claims.text: The target material is Ti-6Al-4V with a conventional untreated microstructure and baseline hardness.
Laser shock peening will be applied at approximately 5 J/cm² per pulse with a protective ablative layer at ambient temperature.
Optimization of pulse overlap, energy density, and spot uniformity will produce a consistently uniform and stable modified surface layer.
Optimized laser shock peening will form a gradient nanocrystalline surface layer on Ti-6Al-4V.
Optimized laser shock peening will induce compressive residual stresses in the near-surface region of Ti-6Al-4V.
Laser shock peening generates intense shock waves that cause severe plastic deformation at the surface.
Severe plastic deformation leads to grain refinement through deformation processes involving slip, twinning, grain-boundary migration, and dislocation structure formation.
Surface severe plastic deformation can create a refined gradient structure accompanied by compressive residual stress.
The nanocrystalline surface structure and compressive residual stresses will increase surface hardness.
The nanocrystalline surface structure and compressive residual stresses will improve resistance to crack initiation and fatigue.
The nanocrystalline surface structure and compressive residual stresses will improve wear resistance.
Laser-shock-peened Ti-6Al-4V will exhibit a 25–40% increase in near-surface hardness relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Laser-shock-peened Ti-6Al-4V will exhibit significantly improved sliding-wear resistance relative to untreated samples.
Laser-shock-peened Ti-6Al-4V will exhibit significantly improved erosive-wear resistance relative to untreated samples.
The treatment will improve performance under high-cycle fatigue conditions relative to untreated samples.
Non-optimized laser parameters may create a non-uniform or unstable nanocrystalline layer.
Excessive laser processing may damage the substrate or cause premature degradation during long-term cyclic loading.
The long-term stability of the induced nanocrystalline structure and compressive stresses under severe service conditions is uncertain.
